paths.description: Homepage/listing template, primary discovery surface, age gate, global navigation, responsive and preference conditions.
Category listing archetype representing filtered browse pages.
Search-results journey reached with a query parameter.
Video-detail/media-player archetype used to inspect metadata and media alternatives.
Authentication and account-creation form archetype, including invalid submission recovery.
Intentional missing route used to test HTTP and recovery behavior.

findings.summary: The page ignores the user’s dark-mode preference.
findings.evidence: Desktop screenshots under light and prefers-color-scheme: dark are visually identical; the CSS probe found no color-scheme, prefers-color-scheme, or light-dark() support.
findings.suggestedFix: Add color-scheme: light dark and theme surfaces, text, controls, and the age gate through prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Navigation swaps views abruptly.
findings.evidence: The CSS probe found no View Transition rules or API styling on an MPA with frequent category, search, account, and detail navigation.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively add @view-transition { navigation: auto } for same-origin MPA navigation and style only meaningful shared elements, with a non-supporting fallback.

findings.summary: Long listings provide no scroll-state guidance.
findings.evidence: The homepage is roughly 4,977 CSS px tall, but CSS inspection found no scroll-state query, progress indicator, or shrinking-header behavior.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a lightweight sticky header state or scroll progress/affordance on long listing pages, preferably with CSS scroll-state/container features and a fallback.

findings.summary: Navigation does not visibly preserve or direct attention.
findings.evidence: Representative links perform full abrupt swaps and the CSS probe found no view-transition, highlight, scroll-marker, or related attention cue.
findings.suggestedFix: Add restrained directional transitions or current-location highlighting to category/search/detail navigation, respecting reduced motion.

findings.summary: The blocking age gate is an unlabelled custom modal.
findings.evidence: DOM evidence shows #disclaimer_message is a DIV with no role or tabindex; the page contains zero dialog or popover elements even though the gate blocks the whole viewport.
findings.suggestedFix: Implement the age gate with <dialog> opened modally, an accessible name/description, initial focus, trapped modal focus, and explicit completion behavior.

findings.summary: Dense chrome competes with the primary content.
findings.evidence: The first viewport contains two full navigation rows, utility controls, category links, badges, and a five-column grid; the screenshot shows limited hierarchy and substantial competing chrome.
findings.suggestedFix: Consolidate secondary navigation behind a clearly labelled disclosure and simplify metadata/badges so titles and thumbnails dominate.

findings.summary: Responsive behavior is viewport-only rather than component-aware.
findings.evidence: The narrow layout does reflow, but the CSS probe found no @container usage despite repeated video cards and navigation components being reused at several widths.
findings.suggestedFix: Use container queries for card metadata and navigation subcomponents where their available inline size, not the viewport, determines layout.

findings.summary: Many interactive targets are too small for touch.
findings.evidence: The rendered-control probe found 124 of 362 visible links/buttons/inputs below 24 px in at least one dimension; Lighthouse also reported accessibility failures. Keyboard focus itself was visible.
findings.suggestedFix: Increase compact links and icon buttons toward 44x44 CSS px hit areas, keep visible focus, and provide non-hover labels/states.

findings.summary: Largest Contentful Paint is slow.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP at 5.43 s (performance 0.75), while the first-party trace measured 2.88 s; the slower throttled result is outside the 2.5 s good threshold.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP candidate, reduce initial thumbnail competition, and remove avoidable critical-path work; verify under Lighthouse throttling and field data.

findings.summary: The mobile listing shifts substantially during load.
findings.evidence: The 360x800 layout observer measured CLS 0.292 across three shifts; 99 of 100 images lacked explicit dimensions.
findings.suggestedFix: Reserve thumbnail and banner space with width/height or aspect-ratio and stabilize late UI before first paint.

findings.summary: The critical path and cache behavior are inefficient.
findings.evidence: HAR evidence recorded 122 requests and 2.89 MB, a parser-blocking head script without async/defer, a 215 KB stylesheet, and many thumbnail responses without cache headers.
findings.suggestedFix: Defer non-critical scripts, split/trim critical CSS, set durable cache headers on versioned thumbnails/assets, and prioritize only above-fold media.

findings.summary: The homepage ships large amounts of unused CSS and JavaScript.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 592,727 bytes of unused JavaScript and 210,257 bytes of unused CSS; HAR shows a 516 KB main script plus duplicate jQuery resources.
findings.suggestedFix: Split bundles by template, remove duplicate jQuery delivery, and conditionally load player/account code only where required.

findings.summary: Core controls and images lack accessible names.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed button-name, link-name, and image-alt; the image audit found 98 of 100 images without alt, and both search inputs lacked labels or aria-label.
findings.suggestedFix: Give search controls explicit labels/names, add names to icon-only buttons and links, and provide meaningful thumbnail alt text or empty alt when adjacent text is equivalent.

findings.summary: Text fails minimum color contrast.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported a color-contrast failure on the audited homepage.
findings.suggestedFix: Adjust the failing text/background tokens to WCAG AA contrast in default, hover, disabled, and forced-colors conditions.

findings.summary: The homepage has no heading hierarchy.
findings.evidence: The DOM and CSS probe found zero h1/h2/h3 elements despite a large content listing; Lighthouse’s agent accessibility tree audit also failed. Focus outlines were visible, but structural navigation is weak.
findings.suggestedFix: Add one descriptive h1 and logical section headings; retain native landmarks and visible focus in DOM reading order.

findings.summary: Listing text is cramped and frequently truncated.
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile screenshots show card titles clipped to fragments and tightly packed metadata, reducing comprehension in both English and RTL layout.
findings.suggestedFix: Allow readable multi-line titles, increase spacing/line-height, and use intentional text wrapping and truncation with an accessible full name.

findings.summary: User zoom and media alternatives are insufficient.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed meta-viewport because scaling is restricted below its accessibility bar; the detail-page video had no text tracks, and 124 controls were below 24 px in one dimension.
findings.suggestedFix: Allow unrestricted pinch zoom, enlarge targets, and provide captions or equivalent transcripts for published video content.

findings.summary: Image markup does not reserve space or use responsive assets.
findings.evidence: The image primitive found 99 images without dimensions, 100 without srcset, and 3 oversized; the document itself had a valid HTML doctype and UTF-8 charset.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit intrinsic width/height, responsive srcset/sizes, and correct aspect ratios for every thumbnail/logo.

findings.summary: Deprecated API use and missing source maps reduce platform hygiene.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse found one deprecated API warning and missing source maps for large first-party JavaScript; BFCache passed and no prompt-on-load was observed.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace the deprecated API and publish production source maps to an access-controlled artifact host or DevTools-compatible endpoint.

findings.summary: Some links are not crawlable.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed crawlable-anchors and found one affected item; the viewport exists but is configured in a way that also failed the zoom audit. robots.txt allows public content.
findings.suggestedFix: Use real href values for navigational controls and retain descriptive link text; do not restrict user scaling.

findings.summary: Public pages omit canonical URLs.
findings.evidence: Both homepage and detail probes returned no rel=canonical. The detail page exposes a different og:url shape, increasing duplicate-URL ambiguity; robots.txt allows crawling.
findings.suggestedFix: Add self-referencing canonical links for indexable templates and keep canonical, Open Graph URL, sitemap, and hreflang signals consistent.

findings.summary: Transport defenses are incomplete and CSP is weak.
findings.evidence: The page uses HTTPS, but headers evidence found no HSTS or X-Content-Type-Options and a CSP permitting unsafe-inline and unsafe-eval across a very broad host allowlist.
findings.suggestedFix: Enable HSTS and nosniff; migrate inline/eval-dependent code to nonce/hash-based CSP and narrow connect/script/image sources by template.

findings.summary: The initial page exposes a broad third-party surface.
findings.evidence: The HAR recorded 101 third-party requests and 1.73 MB from third-party origins, including one non-CDN host; the CSP allowlist includes many advertising/tracking domains even though the tracker matcher found no known tracker.
findings.suggestedFix: Inventory and remove unnecessary third parties, gate advertising/analytics by context and consent, and batch/minimize telemetry.

findings.summary: Authentication is password-only and lacks passkey support.
findings.evidence: The account probe found required email/password fields and no WebAuthn/passkey integration; no permission prompt appeared on load.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer passkey registration and authentication alongside recovery-safe fallback methods, with conditional UI where supported.

findings.summary: Several defensive browser policies are absent or permissive.
findings.evidence: Headers evidence found no Permissions-Policy, no HSTS, no nosniff, a legacy no-referrer-when-downgrade policy, and a session_token cookie using SameSite=None for 180 days. X-Frame-Options was present.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a restrictive Permissions-Policy, strict-origin-when-cross-origin or stricter Referrer-Policy, HSTS/nosniff, and use Lax/Strict for the first-party session cookie unless a documented cross-site flow requires None.

findings.summary: Installability metadata is inconsistent and there is no offline worker.
findings.evidence: The page links a manifest, but its start_url points to https://www.xvideos.com rather than this host, and the service-worker probe found zero registrations.
findings.suggestedFix: Correct the manifest start_url/scope for this origin and provide a minimal service worker with a safe offline shell/fallback for navigation failures.

findings.summary: The Arabic locale mixes English content with RTL without robust logical styling.
findings.evidence: html lang=ar and dir=rtl are present, but screenshots show major navigation, titles, and error text in English; CSS inspection found no logical inline/block properties.
findings.suggestedFix: Complete Arabic translation, mark embedded English spans with lang/dir as needed, and replace physical left/right layout rules with logical properties.

findings.summary: Counts and durations are not localized for the Arabic locale.
findings.evidence: The Arabic page renders English-style compact counts and units such as “41.5k Views” and “min” throughout the screenshot.
findings.suggestedFix: Format counts and durations with Intl.NumberFormat/Intl.DurationFormat or localized message formatting for the active locale.

findings.summary: Sign-in and sign-up fields omit key autocomplete tokens.
findings.evidence: The account probe found empty autocomplete on email/login and current password fields, and on several sign-up identity/password fields; only new-password fields were tokenized.
findings.suggestedFix: Add username/email, current-password, new-password, and appropriate profile tokens so password managers and autofill work reliably.

findings.summary: Image delivery is not resource-efficient.
findings.evidence: Of 100 images, 99 used legacy formats, all lacked srcset, 99 lacked dimensions, and 3 were oversized.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate AVIF/WebP variants, responsive srcset/sizes, and correctly sized thumbnails while retaining a compatible fallback.

findings.summary: The homepage eagerly over-fetches below-fold content.
findings.evidence: The image audit found 90 below-fold images without loading=lazy; HAR loaded 106 images and 2.89 MB during the initial visit.
findings.suggestedFix: Lazy-load below-fold thumbnails, paginate/virtualize long feeds, and defer non-essential fetches until content approaches the viewport.

findings.summary: Third-party and media cost is high before the user chooses content.
findings.evidence: The initial page transferred 1.73 MB from third-party origins across 101 requests, mostly thumbnail CDNs, before a video was selected.
findings.suggestedFix: Apply a first-viewport media budget, lazy-load the rest, consolidate CDN requests where practical, and avoid loading player/media code until intent.
